title: I've factored the RSA keys of a Certificate Authority from the 90s
summary: A security researcher successfully factored RSA keys from a Certificate Authority dating back to the 1990s, demonstrating that legacy cryptographic keys from that era can be broken with modern computational power and factorization techniques.
problem_solved: Demonstrates the practical vulnerability of old 1990s-era RSA keys that may still be in use or cached in systems.
why_valuable: Highlights the critical security risk of legacy cryptographic keys and the necessity of regular key rotation and deprecation of outdated encryption standards.
